selectionReason: debug-handoff.json's 'radio-row-missing-left-padding' failure already diagnosed a confirmed, local root cause with a targeted reproduction: radio-button-group.component.ts's `.rbg > app-radio-button { padding-inline: var(--rbg-padding-x); }` is scoped to the group component's own ViewEncapsulation.Emulated attribute, but the `<app-radio-button>` elements it targets are projected content declared in astronaut-model.component.ts's template and carry that component's `_ngcontent` scope instead, so the descendant selector can never match. No competing hypothesis and no cross-boundary uncertainty, so 'immediate' was used and never a higher tier.

attempts.hypothesis: Confirmed: the `.rbg > app-radio-button` padding rule in radio-button-group.component.ts's own Emulated-encapsulation style scope can never match `<app-radio-button>` elements that astronaut-model.component.ts projects into `<ng-content />`, since those elements carry astronaut-model's `_ngcontent` scope attribute, not radio-button-group's. The same applies to the group's `:hover`/`:active` background rules on the same selector, which were already dead for the same reason but were not part of the named failure and were left untouched.
reproductionEvidence: Static/structural: confirmed by reading the compiled selector's scope requirement against Angular's documented Emulated view-encapsulation behavior for `<ng-content>`-projected elements — a projected element keeps the `_ngcontent` attribute of the component whose template declared it, never the projecting component's, so a parent-scoped descendant selector can only ever match content declared in the parent's own template.
